posts.title: Turnaround Tuesday: Broad Rally Lifts Dow 370 Points as Tech Rebounds
posts.content: U.S. equity markets staged a powerful comeback on Tuesday, with the Dow jumping 370 points (0.76%), the S&P 500 rising 0.77% to 6,890, and the Nasdaq gaining 1.04% to 22,864. The rally was fueled by tech strength, improving consumer confidence, and a relief bounce in AI-related stocks after recent sell-offs. Investors are positioning ahead of Nvidia's earnings tomorrow and Trump's State of the Union address. The market breadth was widespread, with software leading the recovery and AI disruption fears temporarily set aside. This turnaround demonstrates resilience despite ongoing tariff uncertainty.

posts.title: Home Depot Beats Q4 Despite Housing Slump
posts.content: Home Depot (HD) shares rose nearly 4% after posting better-than-expected Q4 results. The company earned $2.72 per share on revenue of $38.2 billion, beating estimates of $2.54 EPS and $38.12B revenue. However, housing market turnover remains near historic lows with sales down 3.8% YoY. Management expects a 'thaw' with existing home sales rising 3-4% as mortgage rates stabilize near 6%. HD maintained its fiscal 2026 forecast of flat to 2% comp sales growth. The results show resilience in consumer home improvement spending even as the housing market struggles.

posts.title: AMD Surges 11% on Historic $60B AI Chip Deal with Meta
posts.content: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) rocketed 11% after announcing a landmark multiyear agreement to supply up to $60 billion worth of AI chips to Meta Platforms over five years. The deal includes provisions for AMD to issue Meta 160 million shares (up to 10% ownership) and covers 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs. This is Meta's largest AI chip purchase to date and validates AMD's MI450 chip in the competitive AI hardware market. The agreement demonstrates sustained demand for AI infrastructure and strengthens AMD's position against Nvidia. Shares had been under pressure earlier in 2026 but this deal repositions AMD as a serious AI infrastructure player.

posts.title: Nvidia Short Interest Hits Record $300B Ahead of Earnings
posts.content: Nvidia (NVDA) short interest has reached a record 265 million shares with a notional value of approximately $300 billion, as bears accumulate positions betting on a pullback after earnings. Despite the massive short positioning, 95% of prediction markets still expect a beat. Major firms like Truist maintain buy ratings, citing AI infrastructure growth and data center demand. Nvidia reports Q4 earnings after the bell on Wednesday, February 25. With the stock carrying the largest short exposure in the S&P 500, any significant move could trigger a short squeeze. The market's reaction to guidance will be crucial for sustaining AI sector momentum.

posts.title: Eli Lilly Poised to Win GLP-1 Race as Novo Nordisk Underperforms
posts.content: Deutsche Bank reiterated a buy rating on Eli Lilly (LLY) with a $1,285 price target, implying 21% upside. The bank believes Lilly is outpacing competitors in the GLP-1 weight loss drug market, citing superior clinical data where tirzepatide users achieved 25.5% weight loss. Novo Nordisk's competing drug has underperformed in comparative studies. The GLP-1 market continues to expand beyond diabetes into obesity treatment, with analysts projecting both companies could capture significant market share. Lilly's innovative pipeline and stronger efficacy profile position it to dominate the next phase of the weight-loss pharmaceutical boom.

posts.title: Consumer Confidence Jumps, Boosting Market Sentiment Ahead of SOTU
posts.content: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose unexpectedly in February, climbing to 102.8 from a revised 97.4 in January. This marks the largest monthly increase in two years and suggests households are feeling more optimistic about the economy despite recent tariff rhetoric and market volatility. The improvement in consumer sentiment buoyed markets on Tuesday, providing a fundamental support for the 'Turnaround Tuesday' rally. Investors are now focused on President Trump's State of the Union address Wednesday night, seeking clarity on trade policy and economic direction. Strong consumer confidence typically bodes well for retail spending and overall economic growth.
